rows.why: Most rows are plain addition that nothing on the list asks about. The open question here is whether zero values are allowed (`0s` → 0, `1d0h0m0s0ms`), which is item 9. Its pick accepts `0s` and parses it to 0, which matches.
Item 3 asks whether whitespace around a duration is allowed. The scenario trims it and returns 2700000. The pick rejects all whitespace and trims nothing.

Several items touch these rows (3 for whitespace, 4 for case, 6 for empty input, 9 for `05s`). Item 5 is closest because most rows are bare, fractional or signed forms (`90`, `1.5h`, `-3s`, `+3s`) and the grammar is 'digits then unit'. Its pick rejects all of these. Note that item 9's pick accepts leading zeros, so it would conflict with the `05s` row.
No item asks whether a count can exceed what the next unit up holds (`90m` on input). Item 2 is about the order of units, and item 11 is about formatting.

Three of the four rows (`30m1h`, `5ms1s`, `1s500ms2s`) are out of descending order, which is item 2's question. Item 1 covers only the repeated-unit rows. Item 2's pick accepts any order, but the scenario rejects these inputs.
Item 8 asks about the maximum and whether it is inclusive. Its pick allows exactly 9007199254740991 ms, which is what the scenario expects.
Item 8 covers the maximum. Its pick rejects totals above 9007199254740991 and rejects counts longer than 16 digits early, so both rows are rejected.

Item 11 asks what formatting style to use. The scenario wants the largest-unit-first compound form (`1m30s`, `1h30m`). The pick chooses the shortest string, giving `90s` and `90m`. Item 10's pick, `0s` for 0, also conflicts with the expected `0ms`.

This is another formatting-style case. Under the shortest-string rule, `9007199254740991ms` and `150119987579m991ms` are both 18 characters, shorter than the expected 20-character `104249991d8h59m991ms`. The tie goes to the single component, so the pick outputs `9007199254740991ms`.
No item asks whether formatting and then parsing must give the number back. That depends on how items 2 and 11 are answered together, but neither one asks it.
Item 12 asks how format_duration treats negative, over-limit, bool and float input. Its pick raises ValueError mentioning 'milliseconds' for all of them, including True and 1.0.
